title: the mountain of herbs
hook: the smell of a mountain on the wind, an army rising, and a peak put back

segments.voice: Yesterday: the mountain of herbs. The plants hid, so Hanuman lifted the whole peak and flew it south like a second sun.

The monkeys still conscious see it first: a light in the northern sky, coming fast. Then they hear Hanuman's roar, and they roar back, weak and astonished. He sets down over the battlefield with a mountain in his hands, trees and rocks and all, glowing in the dark. And before anyone has picked a single leaf, something happens that nobody planned. The wind carries the scent of the herbs out over the field.
screen: `A LIGHT IN THE NORTH.` → `HANUMAN'S ROAR.` → `THE SCENT ON THE WIND.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki, that's all it takes. The smell of the herbs drifts over the fallen, and they rise. Rama and Lakshmana breathe in, the arrows come out of them, and their wounds close. All around them the monkeys and bears get up, shaking themselves as if they'd been asleep. Valmiki goes further: even monkeys who had been killed come back to life. He notes something about the other side, too. The rakshasas who had died didn't rise, because Ravana had ordered his dead thrown into the sea, so the enemy wouldn't see how many he'd lost. A king hiding his losses, and so cutting his own people off from healing: Valmiki lets that detail speak for itself. Then Hanuman does something the famous picture doesn't show. He picks up the mountain again, flies it all the way back north, sets it in its place in the Himalaya, and returns to the camp. The peak was borrowed, not taken. He doesn't keep the prize or put it on display. The emergency is over, so the mountain goes home. In a later telling, the Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas, Bharata shoots Hanuman down over Ayodhya as he carries the mountain. In Valmiki the trip is uninterrupted: north, south, north again, and back before the battle starts.
screen: `THE SCENT ALONE HEALS.` · `EVEN THE FALLEN RISE.` · `RAVANA HID HIS DEAD.` · `THE MOUNTAIN GOES HOME.` · then, large: `BORROWED, NOT TAKEN.`

segments.voice: Breathe in slowly through the nose, as if something healing were on the air, and let each breath reach one tired place in the body. Then, kindly, remember something you borrowed in a hard time, someone's time or patience, and hold it with thanks.
Mrtasanjivani, the herb that revives the dead. Its scent alone lifts the fallen army, and when the work is done, Hanuman carries the peak back home to the Himalaya.
Your line: borrowed, not taken. Next, the same story as most people picture it. Rest well.

howItsDone: Hanuman's flight with the herb mountain is recited and sung in devotion to him, in Valmiki's telling and in later ones such as the Ramcharitmanas.

original.note: Sanskrit mṛtasañjīvanī: the herb that revives the dead, from mṛta, dead, and sañjīvanī, bringing back to life.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman dropped off the mountain and that was the end of it.
what it means: the scent healed the army, and he carried the peak back to where it belonged.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki notes that the rakshasa dead could not rise, because Ravana had them thrown into the sea to hide his losses.

chat.says: Once everyone was healed, what did Hanuman do with the mountain?
options: He flew it back north and set it in its place: borrowed, not taken.
He gave it to Vibhishana as a gift for the future king of Lanka.
He dropped it on Lanka's walls to break open the city's gates.
chat.meaning: When the emergency was over, Hanuman flew the peak back to the Himalaya and set it in place. He didn't keep the prize.

Mrtasanjivani.meaning: the herb that brings the dead back to life

Ayodhya.meaning: Rama's home city in the north

Bharata.meaning: Rama's brother, ruling Ayodhya in his name

Tulsidas.meaning: the poet who wrote the Ramcharitmanas

Ramcharitmanas.meaning: Tulsidas's Hindi retelling of Rama's story

recall: the bright peak, the exiles' first home

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 74 (the herbs' scent heals the army; Ravana's dead in the sea; the peak returned)
Tulsidas, Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kanda (Bharata's arrow and Hanuman at Ayodhya)

notes: Sarga number follows the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Healing by the scent of the herbs, including slain monkeys revived: confirm.
Ravana's order to throw the rakshasa dead into the sea to hide losses: confirm the detail and its placement.
Hanuman returning the peak to the Himalaya in this first episode: confirm.
The Ramcharitmanas episode of Bharata's arrow is placed in the Lanka Kanda; confirm. Some tellings place this herb journey after Lakshmana is struck by Ravana's or Meghanada's spear.
